R061-01.notes: A, C (trumpet is cheap, not sold), D (no argument) all contradicted. 'record of trust' is interpretive but clearly the best fit.

R061-02.notes: 'Not to sell it' kills A; dealer takes stock, owners take cases (B misreads); C unsupported. 'I'll read it' plus 'nobody was going to read the ledger' support D.

R061-03.notes: 'Instead' signals the contrast. C inverts (cheap student model). B and D unsupported.

R061-04.notes: 'drew a neat stroke through it' = line. Distractors are other senses of the word.

R061-05.notes: Stated directly. B borrows 'dented' as a lure.

R061-06.notes: The list is of items that 'had gone out the door and not come back', so the single strike means the rest stayed out. A conflicts with his meticulousness. C conflicts with 'cheap student model'. D: someone could point to 'a line I had not seen him write', but the thirty-year-old dates and the matched 1987 trumpet make D weak.

R061-07.notes: Calm tone ('did not look up') and his thanks to the man support charitable trust. A and D add emotions the passage does not show. B has no support. 'Trusts' slightly overreads a generalization, but no other choice comes close.

R061-08.notes: First person, 'my uncle Arno', and helped all week. D fails because the narrator does not know Arno's thoughts.

R061-09.notes: A is the literal-minded trap. Nothing elsewhere suggests distrust of the narrator, and the ledger is the object he values. B and C have no support.

flags.note: Small ambiguity: in paragraph 4 the narrator reports that Arno 'found a line I had not seen him write', which implies the narrator watched him open the back page during the return, possibly from the ladder. A careful reader might say the narrator first glimpsed the list then, which leans toward C. Paragraph 5 ('I climbed down... and looked at the back page. It was a list...') clearly marks the first real view as after the man left, so B is still best. C is also weakened because the narrator was not 'reading numbers' during the return. Consider changing the stem to 'first read the list' or 'first examined the list'.

R061-10.notes: Sequence: man leaves, Arno goes back to the numbers, narrator climbs down and looks. B.

passage_notes: Possible age/timeline strain (nonblocking): the man was a high school student in 1987 and is 'only a few years younger than Arno', which puts Arno at about 20-25 in 1987 while already lending instruments from the shop. Plausible (he may have been an employee) but a little tight. Paragraph 2 suggests the green ledger was being filled during the count, yet its back page holds entries up to thirty years old. That is reconcilable (an old ledger, or entries copied over), and 'a line I had not seen him write' hints at this, but it could confuse a reader. No item depends on it.
